title: Two-Round Even–Mansour Data–Time Lower Bound
summary: The one-round data–time product lower bound is known, but a dedicated information-theoretic bound for two-round Even–Mansour attacks, including key recovery, remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine and prove a dedicated information-theoretic lower bound relating data complexity $D$ and time complexity $T$ for attacks on two-round Even--Mansour ciphers, explicitly including key-recovery attacks. No such dedicated two-round bound is known. Any key-recovery bound must at least enforce $DT=\Omega(2^n)$, as for the one-round construction, and must respect lower bounds for distinguishing attacks because a distinguishing attack can be derived directly from a key-recovery attack.

scope.domain: Information-theoretic cryptanalysis of two-round Even–Mansour ciphers, including key-recovery and distinguishing attacks.
parameters: n: exponent parameter in the one-round lower-bound baseline
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine and prove a dedicated data–time lower bound for attacks on the two-round construction, including key recovery, that meets the one-round baseline and distinguishing-attack constraints.

citations.label: New Key Recovery Attacks on Minimal Two-Round Even-Mansour Ciphers

progress.summary: The source reports that no dedicated information-theoretic data–time bound is known for the two-round construction. It identifies the one-round product bound and distinguishing lower bounds as necessary constraints on key recovery.
citation_labels: Takanori Isobe et al., New Key Recovery Attacks on Minimal Two-Round Even-Mansour Ciphers
